# Verdict: REVISE ## Summary The `BuggyInfiniteScroll` component implements basic semantic markup (`
    `/`
  • `) and IntersectionObserver-driven pagination, but it completely omits status communication, loading state management, and alternative navigation mechanisms. Automated tools (like axe-core) would report zero violations on this code because standard list tags without attributes pass syntactic rules; however, the component silently fails real assistive technology users by failing to announce asynchronous page updates, omitting `aria-busy` / live regions, and trapping keyboard-only and screen reader users in an unbounded scroll with no keyboard-operable trigger or boundary escape. --- ### Pre-commitment Predictions 1. **Dynamic Content / Live Region Absence**: Screen reader users will have no indication that additional items are loading or have loaded. 2. **Missing Loading State & Busy Indicator**: No `aria-busy="true"` or `role="status"` during fetch lifecycle. 3. **Keyboard & Focus Trap / Unbounded Navigation**: Keyboard users scrolling via Tab/arrows cannot intentionally trigger or bypass subsequent fetches, nor can they reach any content below the infinite scroll (e.g., footer). 4. **Missing Landmarks / Region Identification**: Lack of landmark context or accessible name on the list container. --- ## Findings ### Critical Findings 1. **No programmatic announcement or live region when dynamic items are appended** - **Location**: `BuggyInfiniteScroll.jsx:13-16, 37-43` - **Impacted Group**: Screen reader users (VoiceOver, NVDA, JAWS). - **WCAG / APG Citation**: WCAG 2.2 SC 4.1.3 Status Messages (Level AA); WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices Guide for Dynamic Content & Feed. - **Confidence**: HIGH - **Why this matters**: When the sentinel div (`.scroll-trigger`) intersects and `loadMore()` appends 10 items, DOM mutation occurs silently. Screen reader users navigating the list or reading linearly receive zero auditory feedback that the item count grew or that new items exist. - **Fix**: Add a persistent, polite live region container (`role="status"` or `aria-live="polite"` with `aria-atomic="true"`) outside the list that announces updates (e.g., `"Loaded 10 more items. Total items: 30"`). 2. **Loading state is completely uncommunicated to assistive technology** - **Location**: `BuggyInfiniteScroll.jsx:8-16, 36-46` - **Impacted Group**: Screen reader users, cognitive accessibility users, low vision users. - **WCAG / APG Citation**: WCAG 2.2 SC 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value (Level A); WCAG 4.1.3 Status Messages (Level AA). - **Confidence**: HIGH - **Why this matters**: There is no state variable tracking whether an async fetch is in progress, no visual spinner/indicator, and no `aria-busy="true"` on `.items-list` during fetch operations. Users with cognitive disabilities or slow network connections have no way to know whether data is fetching, failed, or finished. - **Fix**: Introduce `isLoading` state. Apply `aria-busy={isLoading}` to the list or container while fetching, render a visible status message/spinner, and ensure error handling is exposed if fetch fails. ``` ### A11y Evidence Finding finding_id: infinite_scroll_silent_append fingerprint: b47e819d source: BuggyInfiniteScroll.jsx:8-46 wcag_or_apg: WCAG 4.1.3 Status Messages / WAI-ARIA APG Feed Pattern section_508_fpc_context: not in scope severity: CRITICAL perspective_alarms: screen_reader=HIGH, cognitive=MEDIUM, keyboard=MEDIUM evidence: BuggyInfiniteScroll.jsx:13 setItems((prev) => [...prev, ...newItems]); no aria-live region or aria-busy present in DOM tree reproduction_steps: 1. Start VoiceOver/NVDA. 2. Scroll to trigger intersection. 3. Observe silence when 10 new list elements mount. expected_behavior: Screen reader receives a polite announcement notifying how many items loaded or current count. actual_behavior: DOM updates silently without speech synthesis notification or status role emission. trend: new ``` --- ### Major Findings 1. **IntersectionObserver-only triggering denies keyboard-only users predictable control** - **Location**: `BuggyInfiniteScroll.jsx:18-34, 44` - **Impacted Group**: Keyboard-only users, switch control users, screen magnifier users. - **WCAG / APG Citation**: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.1.1 Keyboard (Level A). - **Confidence**: HIGH - **Why this matters**: IntersectionObserver relies purely on viewport intersection. A keyboard-only user tabbing through elements has no explicit, operable control (such as a "Load more items" button) to fetch items intentionally. Furthermore, if content (such as a footer, help links, or disclosures) sits below the scroll trigger, tabbing near the bottom repeatedly triggers automatic loads, creating a functional keyboard barrier to reaching footer content. - **Fix**: Provide a manual fallback "Load More" `` alternative for keyboard and assistive technology users. - **Missing error handling state**: No UI or ARIA communication if `loadMore()` rejects or fails. - **Missing heading or landmark**: No heading (`

    `/`

    `) describing the collection. --- ### Perspective Alarms | Perspective | Alarm Level | Trigger Signal | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **Screen reader** | **HIGH** | Asynchronous DOM changes occur with zero live region announcements or `aria-busy` status. | | **Keyboard-only** | **MEDIUM** | Viewport-intersection trigger makes keyboard control clumsy; risks footer obstruction. | | **Low vision** | **MEDIUM** | Absence of visible loading spinners, progress indications, or visual cues at high zoom. | | **Cognitive** | **MEDIUM** | Silent list lengthening with no loading confirmation or end-of-content boundary. | | **Vestibular & motion** | **LOW** | No automated continuous motion or unprompted parallax scrolling. | | **Auditory access** | **LOW** | No audio or video media streams involved. | | **Environmental contrast** | **LOW** | Component uses generic unstyled elements; check styling when visual CSS is added. | --- ### Multi-Perspective Notes - **Screen reader user**: Navigating with arrow keys or virtual cursor reaches the bottom of the list without notice that new items were added. The user may re-read the page unaware that 10 new items were appended. - **Keyboard-only user**: Cannot directly trigger loading without manually scrolling the viewport (e.g. Page Down), and cannot bypass newly appended content if trying to reach elements underneath. - **Low vision user**: When zoomed to 200–400%, the sentinel element may intersect unexpectedly, triggering multiple fetches with no visual spinner indicating pending network activity. - **Cognitive user**: Unannounced updates and lack of clear boundary ("Item 1 to 20 of 100") causes disorientation regarding progress through the list. --- ## Verdict Justification **Verdict: REVISE** While the component uses native semantic list elements (`
      `, `
    • `), it fails core state communication requirements under WCAG 4.1.3 and WAI-ARIA dynamic feed patterns. Implementing a dedicated live region for count updates, an `aria-busy` indicator during loading states, and an explicit keyboard-operable "Load more" trigger will upgrade the component to **ACCEPT**.
